painLanguage.text: AI voice agents solve some problems well and others badly.
Where it struggles Complex objections, emotional conversations, unusual accents and noisy lines.
AI appointment setting Outbound Your problem is conversion from interest to meeting, not reach.
An agent that cannot recognise an opt-out phrased naturally is a compliance problem running at machine speed.

Latency tolerance by use case LOW TOLERANCE FOR DELAY HIGHER TOLERANCE Outbound sales conversations Appointment reminders Objection handling Surveys and feedback Appointment booking Simple notifications Receptionist and inbound calls Structured qualification Watch for the second-order problem too.
A pilot on a few hundred real records tells you more than any evaluation, because it exposes connect rate, list quality and script problems together.
It also carries a problem that outbound to a fresh list does not.

WHAT IS DRIVING THE COST Connected call time S$200 (47%) Platform or licence fee S$150 (35%) Setup, spread over 12 months S$42 (10%) Unanswered call time S$16 (4%) DNC screening S$12 (3%) Singapore number S$8 (2%) Per-minute bands derived from two voice platforms that publish component pricing, converted at 1 USD = 1.2816 SGD (30 July 2026).

One states an all-in range of US$0.07 to US$0.31 per minute, made up of platform US$0.055, speech synthesis US$0.015 to US$0.040, language model US$0.003 to US$0.160, and telephony US$0.015, with optional add-ons such as knowledge base, denoising, guardrails and PII removal adding up to US$0.025.
A second platform charges US$0.05 per minute plus the same components at cost, which lands in the same range and corroborates the first.
